display_name: Wind Gap Woodruff Vineyard Pinot Noir, Santa Cruz Mountains
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Woodruff Vineyard clings to steep Santa Cruz Mountains slopes above the fog line, its shallow rocky shale and sandstone forcing Pinot Noir vines to dig deep for water and minerals. This 2013 and 2014 Wind Gap bottling turns that struggle into bright red fruit laced with earthy tension. Silver medals from TEXSOM highlight its polish without excess weight.",
  "wine_summary": "Wind Gap carved a niche bottling site-specific Pinots from overlooked Santa Cruz Mountains vineyards like Woodruff, where elevation and ocean winds deliver California's coolest mountain fruit. Producer Pax Mahle chased transparency over power, letting fractured geology and diurnal swings dictate the wine's lively structure. These vintages stand out in a region spanning 480,000 acres across three counties, where 85% of grapes must hail from the AVA per federal rules.",
  "terroir_expression": "Shale and sandstone soils, remnants of ancient seabeds uplifted into steep ridges, drain fast and impart a gritty mineral backbone that echoes in the wine's ferrous edge and persistent earth notes. Morning marine fog at 400-3,000 feet elevation cools nights for sharp acidity, while afternoon sun ripens berries to pure raspberry and sappy herb flavors without the jam of warmer sites. Pacific gaps funnel cool air, yielding taut Pinots that taste of the mountains' vertical complexity.",
  "vinification_summary": "Wind Gap ferments with a mix of whole clusters—stems adding savory grip and structure—using native yeasts in open-top vessels to extract gentle color and amplify site details. Aged in neutral French oak, the wine avoids new wood's vanilla mask, preserving the vineyard's raw voice. Whole-cluster inclusion boosts aromatic lift through polymerization, where stem tannins soften into fine grain over time.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled quail with chanterelles matches the wine's earthy shale notes and stemmy herbs to the mushrooms' umami. Nashville hot chicken's spice cuts through bright acidity while red fruit tempers heat. Coq au vin lets ferrous minerality mirror the dish's reduced sauce. Duck confit with lentil salad pairs stem tannins to crispy fat and the wine's sappy depth to legumes. Charcuterie of soppressata and cornichons highlights raspberry against cured pork's brine.",
  "comparable_wines": "Rhys Horseshoe Vineyard Pinot Noir — shared Santa Cruz Mountains fog and rocky soils yield similar high-toned red fruit with mineral drive. Mount Eden Vineyard Pinot Noir — steep slope shale concentration mirrors Woodruff's tense earth and bright core. Calera Mount Harlan Pinot Noir — cool-climate elevation swings produce parallel vibrant acidity and sappy herbs.",
  "style_profile": "Pinot Noir medium body with fine stem tannins and ferrous earth",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2013 now through 2028; 2014 holds to 2029 if stored cool at 55°F. Decant an hour for stem integration.",
  "value_assessment": "$45-65 retail. Stack it against Rhys Alamont Pinot at $55-70, which trades brighter lift for less earth. Worth seeking for SCM purity at this price—silver medals back the quality without Napa markup.",
  "market_position": "Pinot geeks and somms chase it for natural wine lists in San Francisco spots like Zuni Cafe. Retail in specialty shops for California cool-climate collectors. Casual drinkers skip it for broader Burgundies.",
  "insider_take": "SCM Pinots like Woodruff crush budget Burgundy imports on site transparency but demand patience for stem evolution. Skip if you crave plush fruit—its tension rewards food over sipping. Buy multiples if mountain minerality hooks you.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 20,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
    "tannin": 3,
    "body": 3,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 3,
    "color_intensity": "medium",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "long",
    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "very_good"
  }
}
